items.title: George Wein interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: You were not Dr. Wein’s son.

ctx.x: I bet you weren’t alone in that feeling too.

Oh everybody did. But the thing I learned in the Army that was, hey, you were only yourself. You were not Dr. Wein’s son. You were not a nice Jewish kid from a middle class family. Economics, background, nothing meant anything except you, yourself. And you had to compete with the other guy. Now the other guy might have been a brilliant guy from Harvard, he might have been some poor guy from the mountains in Kentucky, he might have been a tough mug from the factories somewhere in Detroit. You had to be equal with…
A lot of the musicians I’ve talked to have been fortunate that they were musicians, much like yourself.
